title: Check yourself: where did the log entry go

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A teammate's 10_host_channel.xml has logger="Q2" on <channel-adaptor> and no logger attribute on the <channel> inside it. 00_logger.xml has ProtectedLogListener first. The host rejected three purchases at 14:02. What does your log hold for those three exchanges?

options.text: Send and receive events under the adaptor's realm, since the adaptor's logger also serves the channel inside it
options.says: the adaptor's logger attribute covers only the adaptor's own events; the channel is a separate component

options.text: Send and receive events under the realm Q2.system, since an event that has no logger falls back to Q2
options.says: only an event with no source falls back to Q2; the channel is the source of its events, and with no logger it drops them

options.text: No events from the channel, since a channel that Q2 gave no logger discards everything it logs
options.says: Q2 calls setLogger only when the element has a logger attribute; without it the channel's events go nowhere

options.text: No events from the channel, since a channel writes events only when a send or a receive fails
options.says: a channel with a logger writes connect, send and receive events for every message, not only for failures

origin.section: 8.2 An Event Goes to Its Source's Logger, and a Channel Without One Writes Nothing

questions.stem: To follow one link, you put a RealmLogFilter, with no dump-interval, after ProtectedLogListener with <enabled>host-channel client.sender</enabled>. An hour later a colleague deploys a 20_host_mux.xml with a typo in its class name. What does the log show about that deployment?

options.text: Nothing, since the filter drops the Q2.system events for every listener that comes after it
options.says: Q2 reports deploy failures under Q2.system; the filter returns null for realms it doesn't name, and the chain stops

options.text: Nothing, since Q2 reports a descriptor that fails to deploy only while the node is starting
options.says: Q2 watches deploy/ and reports a failed deployment whenever it happens

options.text: The deploy error, since events in the Q2.system realm pass through any realm filter
options.says: the filter compares every realm with its list; Q2.system gets no exception

options.text: The deploy error, since a realm filter acts only on events that carry an ISO message
options.says: the filter looks only at the realm, whatever the event carries

origin.section: 8.5 A Realm Filter Narrows the Log and Drops Everything It Doesn't Name

questions.stem: Your request for STAN 018240 returned null after 30 seconds, and the host says it approved it at second 31. The QMUX has a queue configured for leftover messages and no request listener, and the channel has no logger attribute. Where on your side can you see that the approval arrived?

options.text: In an event under the QMUX's realm, since QMUX writes an event for every answer that arrives too late
options.says: QMUX writes no event for an unmatched answer; it only counts it (and with no channel logger nothing else logs it)

options.text: In an event under the sender's realm, since QMUX passes a late answer to the request it belonged to
options.says: the request already returned null; the late answer finds nobody waiting for its key

options.text: In a QMUX counter, since QMUX counts an answer that nobody waits for instead of logging it
options.says: the answer goes to the <unhandled> queue and rx_unhandled counts it; SystemMonitor (detailRequired) prints the counters

options.text: In a QMUX counter, since QMUX counts an answer that comes too late as an expired request
options.says: rx_expired counts requests that ended with no answer; a late answer goes to the unhandled queue and is counted in rx_unhandled

origin.section: 8.6 A Late Answer Is Counted, Not Logged, by the MUX

questions.stem: Your client runs on Java 21 with no SLF4J binding on the classpath and is started with java -cp "lib/*" org.jpos.q2.Q2. A library it uses logs a warning through SLF4J. Where does that warning end up?

options.text: In the Q2 log under a realm named after the library's logger, since Q2 binds SLF4J to its own logger when it starts
options.says: on a current JDK Q2's binding attempt fails with an InaccessibleObjectException unless the JVM opens java.lang

options.text: In the Q2 log under Q2's own system realm, since Q2 collects whatever the libraries in its JVM write
options.says: Q2 does not collect library output by itself; only its SLF4J binding would, under slf4j:: realms

options.text: Nowhere, since Q2's binding attempt fails and SLF4J then uses a logger that discards everything
options.says: Q2 swallows the exception and SLF4J uses its no-operation logger

options.text: Nowhere, since library output reaches the Q2 log only through a bridge listener that forwards it
options.says: a bridge listener carries jPOS events into SLF4J, the other direction

origin.section: 8.7 A Bridge to SLF4J Sits After the Filter and Keeps Each Event Whole

concepts: The channel inside an adaptor logs only with its own logger attribute, and a node without 00_logger.xml writes everything to the console unmasked.
QMUX writes no event for an answer nobody waits for; it counts it in rx_unhandled, which SystemMonitor prints with the other counters.
RealmLogFilter compares the realm before the first slash exactly and stops the chain for every realm it doesn't name, Q2.system included.
A bridge into SLF4J is a writer after the filter that keeps events whole; Q2's own SLF4J binding fails quietly on a current JDK without --add-opens.
